hypothesis:
Retry after a guard false positive, not a redesign. The first attempt was killed at step 105 for running 6.56 steps/s against the throughput guard's 8.0 floor -- while reporting MFU 41.4%, higher than the champion's healthy 39.8%. A 13-layer model legitimately does about 8% more work per step, so it is slow AND efficient; a contended run is slow AND inefficient, at 28.8%. The guard watched step rate, which cannot separate those, and burned the coordinate. It now watches MFU, validated by replay against the real logs: it still aborts t0451 and t0453 and now allows this trial and the MLP 5x arm.

Retest depth 13. It was explored at 8/10/11/12/13/14 early in the campaign and 12 held, but that verdict is old: the champion is 3% better than the model those trials ran against, and it has since gained value embeddings on every layer, the attention gate, four reshaped decay schedules, warmdown 0.7 and max-autotune. **A closed axis can reopen when the operating point moves**, and this one has moved further than any other in the campaign.

There is a specific reason to look again rather than a general one. The MLP bracket measured capacity directly for the first time: adding width gained -0.002872 while removing it cost +0.006633, so capacity is binding and strongly convex. Depth is the other way to buy capacity, and it was last priced when nobody knew what capacity was worth here.

I should be honest that my own arithmetic says this probably loses. A 13th layer adds roughly 8% to per-step FLOPs, which the token law debits at about +0.0045, against a capacity gain I would estimate near -0.0035 by analogy to the MLP arm. That nets positive, i.e. a loss. The estimate is an extrapolation across axes, which is exactly the kind of transfer that has failed me repeatedly today, so it is worth one measurement rather than a conclusion.
change_summary: DEPTH 12 -> 13, one constant. Compile mode also reverts to default, because depth changes the graph and a cache miss under max-autotune exceeds the 660s wall clock -- the failure that killed t0434, t0435, t0436 and t0438. Everything else is the champion's. Dry-run verified. Source differs from the aborted attempt by a comment recording the false positive, which makes it a distinct coordinate -- a guard abort writes a failed record and burns the hash.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Steps should fall by roughly 8% from the extra layer, on top of the ~2.2% the compile revert forfeits, so I expect around 2520-2560 steps against the control's 2744. The token law then debits about +0.0045 relative to the control, and the capacity credit is the residual.
The measurement I actually want is that residual, not the verdict. If it comes in near -0.0035, capacity transfers across axes at roughly the rate the MLP arm implied, which would let me price future capacity changes without running them. If it is much smaller, depth buys less capacity per FLOP than width does, and the model's shape preference is specific rather than a general appetite for parameters.
risk:
I expect this to lose, so the slot is bought for the capacity-per-FLOP number rather than for a promotion. That is a defensible trade only because the queue was empty ten minutes ago and cost a slot to an agent_error -- an expected-loss trial that yields a calibration number strictly beats no trial at all.
A 13th layer also changes every Muon shape group's membership and adds a value-embedding table, so this is not a pure FLOPs change; the capacity residual will bundle the extra table with the extra block and I cannot separate them here.
